1.title: New names for captives
1.text: The four young men were given Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abed-nego — a common way captors tried to absorb the conquered into their culture.

1.question: What did the king appoint for the young men of Judah (Daniel 1:5)?
options: A daily provision of the king's meat and wine
A daily portion of roasted meat and fruit from the king's table
A place of honor beside the princes of Babylon
A sum of silver for their personal expenses

1.question: Why was the prince of the eunuchs afraid to let Daniel skip the king's food (Daniel 1:10)?
options: He feared the king would discover their disobedience and expel him from the palace
He feared their faces would look worse and endanger his own head
He feared the other captive youths would demand the same special treatment
He feared losing Nebuchadnezzar's favor before the whole court

1.question: How much better did the king find these four in wisdom than all the magicians (Daniel 1:20)?
options: Twice better
Five times better
Ten times better
A hundred times better

2.title: A dream they could not even hear
2.text: Nebuchadnezzar demanded the wise men tell him the dream itself, not just its meaning. They protested it was impossible — setting the stage for Daniel.

2.question: What did the king threaten the wise men with if they could not tell the dream (Daniel 2:5)?
options: To be cut in pieces and their houses made a dunghill
To be banished from the kingdom and stripped of all their goods
To be cast into prison for life without any trial
To lose their offices and have their families exiled

2.question: What reason did the Chaldeans give that no one could reveal the dream (Daniel 2:11)?
options: That the astrologers needed seven days to consult the stars
Only the gods could, whose dwelling is not with flesh
That such a mystery was kept in the ancient records of the priests
That only the king himself could recall the dream

2.question: What did Daniel ask the king for, before interpreting (Daniel 2:16)?
options: That Arioch be summoned once more
That he would give him time
That the other wise men be pardoned
That he be given some gold

2.question: According to Daniel's praise, what does God do with kings (Daniel 2:21)?
options: He multiplies riches and diminishes armies
He grants long life to faithful kings
He removeth kings, and setteth up kings
He judges the foreign nations

2.question: What did Daniel say the king saw standing before him in the dream (Daniel 2:31)?
options: A great and terrible image
An army marching against Babylon
A huge serpent rising to the sky
An angel with a flaming sword

2.question: What struck the image's feet and broke them to pieces (Daniel 2:34)?
options: A stone cut out without hands
A hammer forged by the angels
A flame that fell from heaven
A sudden violent earthquake

2.question: In the dream, what was the head of the great image made of (Daniel 2:32)?
options: Silver
Brass
Iron
Fine gold

2.question: After the interpretation, what did the king make Daniel (Daniel 2:48)?
options: Supreme commander of all the king's armies
Personal counselor and royal scribe of the palace
Ruler over the whole province of Babylon
Crown prince of the Babylonian throne

3.title: An image of gold
3.text: Nebuchadnezzar's golden image was 'threescore cubits' high and 'six cubits' broad — about 27 meters tall, set up on the plain of Dura in Babylon for all the realm to worship at the sound of music.

3.question: What was the penalty for not falling down to worship the image (Daniel 3:6)?
options: To be bound and left exposed under the desert sun
To be cast into a burning fiery furnace
To be imprisoned forever in the city's highest tower
To lose all their possessions, offices, and family

3.question: What signaled the people to fall down and worship the golden image (Daniel 3:5,7)?
options: The sound of the cornet, flute, harp, and all kinds of musick
A smoke signal raised high atop the royal tower of the palace
The solemn reading aloud of the decree by the king's priests
The solemn toll of a bronze bell in the main square

3.template: in his rage and fury commanded to bring {0}, Meshach, and Abed-nego

3.question: What did the three say even if God did not deliver them (Daniel 3:18)?
options: That they would keep praying to the God of Israel in secret every night
They still would not serve his gods nor worship the image
That they would beg the king's pardon and offer sacrifices to his gods
That they would rather die than betray the whole people of Judah

3.question: Why was Nebuchadnezzar astonied, asking his counsellors a question (Daniel 3:24)?
options: He saw that the furnace had suddenly gone completely out
He remembered casting only three men bound into the fire
He heard strange voices coming from atop the royal palace
He noticed that the fire had suddenly changed color

3.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar do for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego at the end (Daniel 3:30)?
options: Promoted them in the province of Babylon
Gave them lands and riches throughout the empire
Appointed them supreme counselors over all the satraps
Built them a temple of their own in the city

4.title: A king's own testimony
4.text: Chapter 4 is unusual: it is framed as a public decree written by Nebuchadnezzar himself, addressed 'unto all people, nations, and languages,' telling how the Most High humbled him.

4.question: Why did Nebuchadnezzar call for the wise men of Babylon (Daniel 4:5)?
options: He had a dream which made him afraid
He wanted to build a new temple in his honor
He wanted to choose new counselors to better rule the kingdom
He feared an imminent foreign invasion

4.question: What did the king see in the midst of the earth in his vision (Daniel 4:10)?
options: A great statue with a head of gold
A numerous army marching across the plain
A tree whose height was great
A river overflowing its banks

4.template: leave the {0} of his roots in the earth

4.question: Who alone was finally able to interpret the dream (Daniel 4:18-19)?
options: An angel who came down from heaven only for him
One of the oldest Chaldean wise men of the court
A foreign diviner named Rabshakeh
Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar

4.question: Daniel said the king would be restored after he knew what (Daniel 4:26)?
options: That the heavens do rule
That he was a god on earth
That his power was eternal
That he was invincible

4.question: What boast was in the king's mouth when the voice fell from heaven (Daniel 4:30-31)?
options: That he had subdued all the nations of the earth with his mighty arm and sword
That he had built great Babylon by his power for his majesty
That he would reign forever over all peoples, nations, and tongues of the whole earth
That he had risen to the heavens to rule all the kingdoms

4.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar finally say of those that walk in pride (Daniel 4:37)?
options: That God always rewards the powerful
That the proud prosper forever
That God is able to abase them
That they rule the earth without end

5.title: The temple vessels profaned
5.text: Belshazzar's great sin was bringing out the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, to drink wine from them while praising idols — turning sacred things to mockery.

5.question: While they drank from the temple vessels, whom did they praise (Daniel 5:4)?
options: The gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone
To the God of Israel whom their fathers had served of old
To the spirits of the rivers and mountains of the land
To the ancestors of the king who were buried there

5.question: How did the king and his lords react to the hand that wrote on the wall (Daniel 5:6,9)?
options: The lords laughed and toasted joyfully to the king's health
The king was greatly troubled and his countenance changed
The king ordered music and dancing for his whole royal court
The lords noticed nothing throughout that whole night

5.question: Why was Daniel finally brought before Belshazzar (Daniel 5:12-13)?
options: He was a valiant soldier who had defended the royal palace
He was a close relative of King Belshazzar at that time
He could interpret dreams and dissolve doubts
He was the owner of all the vessels of gold and silver

5.question: What happened to Nebuchadnezzar when his heart was lifted up in pride (Daniel 5:20)?
options: He was crowned again with great honor and glory
He grew even richer and more powerful than before
He conquered new lands for his vast empire
He was deposed from his kingly throne

5.question: Who took the kingdom after Belshazzar was slain (Daniel 5:30-31)?
options: Darius the Median
Cyrus the Persian
Nebuchadnezzar
Arioch

6.question: Where did Daniel's rivals decide they could find occasion against him (Daniel 6:5)?
options: Concerning the law of his God
In his dealings with the poor
In his management of the royal treasury
In his own private life

6.title: A law that could not be changed
6.text: The plotters used 'the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not' — once King Darius signed the decree, not even he could undo it, which is exactly how they trapped him into condemning Daniel.

6.question: When Daniel knew the writing was signed, what did he do (Daniel 6:10)?
options: He fled the city and hid in the distant mountains for thirty days
He kneeled and prayed three times a day, as he did aforetime
He hid in his house and would not open the windows for anyone to see
He went to the king to beg mercy for his whole people

6.question: How did the conspirators catch Daniel breaking the decree (Daniel 6:11)?
options: They bribed his servants so that they would quickly report on him
They followed him all the way to the royal palace and watched him enter
They found him praying and making supplication before his God
They intercepted a private letter he had secretly written

6.template: and laid upon the mouth of the {0}

6.question: What did Daniel tell the king when he was found alive (Daniel 6:21-22)?
options: That he had bribed the guards of the den throughout the night
That the lions had been tame and gentle for a very long time
That he had escaped through a back door in the night
That God had sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths

6.question: How did Daniel fare after this, according to Daniel 6:28?
options: He prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus
He returned to Judah and rebuilt the temple of the Lord there again
He retired from royal service and lived in peace until his death
He was imprisoned again by the order of his jealous rivals

7.title: Beasts from the sea
7.text: Daniel's night vision of four great beasts rising from the storm-tossed sea parallels the four-metal image of chapter 2: both picture a succession of earthly kingdoms, but this time as wild beasts.

7.question: What was the first beast like, and what did it have (Daniel 7:4)?
options: Like a lion, with eagle's wings
Like a bear, with three ribs
Like a leopard, with four wings
Like an ox, with iron horns

7.question: Whose throne was like the fiery flame, with wheels as burning fire (Daniel 7:9)?
options: The little horn's
The fourth beast's
The Ancient of days'
Belshazzar's

7.template: the judgment was set, and the {0} were opened

7.question: When one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, what was given him (Daniel 7:13-14)?
options: A throne of fire and a book of judgment opened before him
Dominion, glory, and a kingdom that shall not be destroyed
Power over the four beasts and dominion over all the earth
Wisdom and strength to judge all the kingdoms of the earth

7.question: What did Daniel learn the four great beasts represent (Daniel 7:17)?
options: Four kingdoms that would endure forever without end
Four prophets sent to proclaim judgment upon the earth
Four kings, which shall arise out of the earth
Four guardian angels of the nations of the earth

7.question: What did the little horn do to the saints, until the Ancient of days came (Daniel 7:21-22)?
options: Fled from them and hid himself in the mountains
Made a covenant with them and gave them great power
Served them and obeyed them in all things
Made war with them, and prevailed against them

7.question: How did Daniel feel at the end of the matter (Daniel 7:28)?
options: His thoughts much troubled him, and his countenance changed
He felt great peace and joy, and told the vision to all the people of Babylon
He was filled with confidence and wrote the vision with great rejoicing in his heart
He laughed at the vision and returned calmly to his daily tasks

8.question: What animal did Daniel see standing before the river, with two high horns (Daniel 8:3)?
options: A ram
A lion
A bear
A he goat

8.title: A horn against the host of heaven
8.text: Out of the goat's four horns rose a 'little horn' that magnified itself even against 'the host of heaven,' casting down some of the stars — vivid imagery of a power that exalts itself against God's people and worship.

8.question: Where did the he goat come from, touching not the ground (Daniel 8:5)?
options: From the north
From the west
From the east
From the sea

8.question: Who was called by name to make Daniel understand the vision (Daniel 8:16)?
options: Michael
Belteshazzar
Gabriel
Arioch

8.question: According to Gabriel, what did the rough goat represent (Daniel 8:21)?
options: The king of Egypt
The king of Babylon
The kings of Media and Persia
The king of Grecia

8.question: How did Daniel react after the vision, in Daniel 8:27?
options: He fainted, was sick certain days, and was astonished at the vision
He rejoiced greatly and called all the people together to celebrate the victory
He wrote a song of praise and gathered the wise men to interpret the dream
He went immediately to war against the king of the north and south

9.title: Reading the prophets
9.text: Daniel understood 'by books' that Jeremiah had foretold seventy years of desolation for Jerusalem — a striking case of one prophet studying the written words of another, and praying over what he read.

9.question: What did Daniel confess his people had done (Daniel 9:5)?
options: Sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled
Kept all the commandments and walked faithfully in the laws of the Lord
Honored the prophets and offered sacrifices according to the law of Moses
Built the temple and restored worship in the sanctuary

9.question: What did Daniel say had been done upon Jerusalem (Daniel 9:12)?
options: A great feast, such as had never been seen in all the land of Israel
A great evil, such as had not been done under the whole heaven
A solemn coronation, such as never was among the kings of the earth
A treaty of peace that would last forever between the nations

9.question: What did Daniel ask God to cause to shine upon his desolate sanctuary (Daniel 9:17)?
options: His face
His sword
His fire
His banner

9.question: Who came to Daniel to give him skill and understanding (Daniel 9:21-22)?
options: Michael
An unnamed watcher
A son of the king
The man Gabriel

9.question: How many weeks did Gabriel say are determined upon Daniel's people and holy city (Daniel 9:24)?
options: Seventy weeks
Forty weeks
Twelve weeks
A hundred weeks

10.title: By the great river
10.text: The vision came as Daniel stood 'by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel' — the Hebrew name for the Tigris, one of the rivers flowing through ancient Mesopotamia where the captives lived.

10.question: How is the man Daniel saw described in Daniel 10:5-6?
options: Clothed in linen, his face as lightning and his eyes as lamps of fire
Wearing a crown of fine gold, with royal robes and a silver scepter in hand
Riding a chariot of fire, surrounded by burning wheels and great flames
Bearing a shining sword and a great shield of polished bronze

10.question: How did the messenger address Daniel (Daniel 10:11)?
options: Son of man, arise and hear my words
O Daniel, a man greatly beloved
Blessed art thou, chosen of the Lord
Faithful servant, fear no more

10.template: by the {0} my sorrows are turned upon me

10.question: Who is named as Daniel's prince, holding with the messenger (Daniel 10:21)?
options: Gabriel
Cyrus
The prince of Persia
Michael

11.title: Three kings, then a fourth
11.text: The messenger foretells 'three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all,' who would 'stir up all against the realm of Grecia' — the long prophecy of chapter 11 traces a chain of rulers in remarkable detail.

11.question: Which two rivals does Daniel 11:5 introduce, whose long war the prophecy traces?
options: The king of the south and one of his princes
The king of the north and one of the princes of Greece
The king of Persia and the valiant king who would reign with great dominion
The fourth king of Persia and the king of Greece

11.question: What does Daniel 11:10 say his sons shall do?
options: Make peace with the king of the south and end the wars forever
Be stirred up and assemble a multitude of great forces
Flee to the isles of the sea and abandon their father completely
Abandon the war and surrender to the king of the north

11.question: What does Daniel 11:16 say of him that comes against the king of the south?
options: He shall be utterly defeated and never rise again against the south lands
He shall make peace with the king of the south and seal an eternal treaty between them
He shall do according to his own will, and none shall stand before him
He shall turn back and abandon completely the conquest of the land

11.question: Who, besides the overflowing forces, shall be broken in Daniel 11:22?
options: The high priest of the temple
The governor of the northern fortress
The son of the king of the south
The prince of the covenant

11.template: he shall come up, and shall become strong with a small {0}

11.question: When the king returns to his land with great riches, against what is his heart (Daniel 11:28)?
options: The holy covenant
His own princes
The king of the north
The city of Babylon

11.question: What does Daniel 11:33 say of those that understand among the people?
options: They flee to the mountains and hide themselves from their enemies' pursuit for many days
They instruct many, yet fall by sword, flame, captivity, and spoil
They are made kings over the nations and receive great honor among all the people of the land
They hide in caves to flee from the pursuit of the king of the north

11.question: What does Daniel 11:36 say the king will do against the God of gods?
options: Worship him with sacrifices all his days
Build him a magnificent temple in Jerusalem
Speak marvellous things against him
Offer him daily sacrifices forever

11.question: What does Daniel 11:38 say the king will honour in his estate?
options: The God of his fathers
The desire of women
The prophets
The god of forces

11.question: How does Daniel 11:45 say this king will finally end?
options: He shall come to his end, and none shall help him
He shall reign forever over all the nations of the earth
He shall repent of his sins and turn to the true God
He shall flee to the isles and live in peace until death

12.title: A clear word on resurrection
12.text: Daniel 12:2 — 'many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame' — is one of the clearest Old Testament statements of the resurrection of the dead.

12.question: What was Daniel told to do with the words, until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4)?
options: Shut up the words, and seal the book
Rewrite the words into an entirely new book
Proclaim the words to the whole kingdom
Translate them into another language

12.question: How long did the man clothed in linen swear it would be (Daniel 12:7)?
options: Forty whole days and forty whole nights
Three whole times and half of two times
A time, times, and an half
Seventy years of complete captivity

12.question: What was promised to Daniel at the very end of the book (Daniel 12:13)?
options: An eternal throne on earth and dominion over all the nations of the world
Countless riches and a place of honor beside the king of Babylon
Long life and prosperity for his whole family and descendants
Rest, and to stand in his lot at the end of the days
